newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSG sees late summer rise in nickel offtake.
newsitem.headline: INSG sees late summer rise in nickel offtake.

text.p: Western world nickel consumption edged up slightly in August and September to 70,000 and 71,200 tonnes respectively against 69,500 in July, the International Nickel Study Group (INSG) said in its latest bulletin.
One of the main factors was a steady rise in Japanese offtake to 15,500 and 16,000 tonnes from 15,100 in July. Consumption elsewhere was largely static.
Data showed primary nickel output also rising in the latest two months to be surveyed.
INSG pegged western world production of primary metal at 54,100 and 56,900 tonnes against 51,000 in July.
The main reason was a return to more normal output in Canada after a dip in July related to summer shutdowns.
Production there was given at 9,700 and 10,000 tonnes for August and September against just 3,000 in July.
However, levels are still not back to the year's peak of 12,800 tonnes reached in May.
European output remained relatively steady as a whole.

French production returned to a more normal 1,200 tonnes in September against zero in July, but this was offset by a continuing drop in Finnish figures, which fell to 2,100 and 2,000 tonnes in August and September from 3,300 in July.
